items.title: [Launched] Generally Available: Managed StandardV2 NAT Gateway for AKS
items.headline: AKS-managed StandardV2 NAT Gateway is now GA and the default for managed NAT egress
items.summary: AKS can now provision and manage a StandardV2 NAT Gateway for clusters that use an AKS-managed virtual network. StandardV2 becomes the default managed NAT Gateway SKU for new clusters in supported regions when the managedNATGateway outbound type is used.
items.architecture_impact: New AKS clusters that use managed NAT egress get the StandardV2 SKU by default, so revisit egress topology and resilience assumptions against the current managed NAT pattern. The differences from Standard NAT Gateway, such as zone behaviour, throughput and pricing, and the list of supported regions are not in the item and need checking at the source.

items.title: Retirement: Microsoft Dev Box will be retired on September 18, 2028
items.headline: Microsoft Dev Box will be retired on September 18, 2028
items.summary: Microsoft Dev Box will retire on September 18, 2028 and is currently in maintenance mode. The closing-down process begins September 14, 2026, and after retirement the service will no longer be available.
items.architecture_impact: Organisations using Dev Box for managed developer workstations need to choose an alternative platform and plan the migration well before the retirement date. Stop designing new solutions on Dev Box. The recommended alternative is not in the item and needs checking at the source.

items.title: Retirement: Azure Deployment Environments will be retired on February 22, 2027
items.headline: Azure Deployment Environments will be retired on February 22, 2027
items.summary: Azure Deployment Environments will retire on February 22, 2027, with the closing-down process starting September 14, 2026. After retirement the service will no longer be available.
items.architecture_impact: Platform engineering designs that rely on Deployment Environments for self-service, template-based environment provisioning must move to another mechanism, such as pipeline-driven IaC, within a short window. The recommended migration path is not in the item and needs checking at the source.

items.title: Retirement: Azure App Service on Azure Stack Hub
items.headline: Azure App Service on Azure Stack Hub will be retired on September 30, 2029
items.summary: Azure App Service on Azure Stack Hub retires on September 30, 2029. From September 30, 2026, new installations are no longer supported and no new releases, features or enhancements will ship.
items.architecture_impact: Hybrid and edge designs that host web apps on Stack Hub App Service need a replacement hosting model, such as containers on Kubernetes, and should not be extended. The supported migration targets are not in the item and need checking at the source.

items.title: Build and govern AI agents across a multitenant organization
items.headline: Federated agent factory for building and governing AI agents across tenants
items.summary: The guidance addresses enterprises operating hundreds of AI agents across subsidiaries with separate Microsoft Entra tenants, data and regulatory obligations. It proposes a federated model: Agent 365 provides central inventory and governance, while agent identities, data, detailed telemetry and runtime enforcement stay local to each tenant. It relies partly on preview capabilities, including Entra Tenant Governance, multitenant agent management and the API Management AI Gateway tier.
items.architecture_impact: Centralize standards and oversight, not tenant data, so a central failure cannot become a cross-subsidiary leak. Give every agent its own Entra Agent ID, published from multitenant blueprints as tenant-local identities. Expose narrow, versioned tools through governed APIs or MCP servers, and enforce policy at runtime with evaluation and observability treated as core operations; the reliance on preview components and their regional availability needs checking.

items.title: Retirement: Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3, and Esv3 Azure VMs
items.headline: Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3 and Esv3 VM series to retire on November 15, 2029
items.summary: Under the Azure VM lifecycle policy, Microsoft is retiring the Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3 and Esv3 VM series in public cloud regions, and they now enter the End-of-Life stage. Retirement is scheduled for November 15, 2029, and affects any workload still running on these widely used sizes.
items.architecture_impact: Inventory your Dv3/Ev3-family VMs, scale sets and IaC templates, and plan to move them to newer series before November 15, 2029; recommended target series and any purchase restrictions need checking at the source. New designs and reservation renewals should avoid these sizes.

items.title: [Launched] Generally Available: SQL Server on Azure Local Disconnected (ALDO)
items.headline: SQL Server on Azure Local Disconnected Operations (ALDO) is generally available
items.summary: SQL Server support now extends to Azure Local running in disconnected operations (ALDO). This targets highly regulated, secure, remote or air-gapped environments where continuous connectivity to Azure is not possible.
items.architecture_impact: Sovereign, defence and edge designs can now standardize on Azure Local with SQL Server without depending on a connection to Azure. Feature parity, licensing and management differences from connected deployments need checking at the source.

items.title: Retirement: Azure Arc enabled System Center Virtual Machine Manager will be retired September 30, 2029
items.headline: Azure Arc-enabled SCVMM to be retired on September 30, 2029
items.summary: Microsoft is retiring Azure Arc-enabled System Center Virtual Machine Manager on September 30, 2029. Customers using it to project and manage SCVMM-hosted VMs through Azure must transition to alternative solutions.
items.architecture_impact: Hybrid management designs that rely on Arc-enabled SCVMM for Azure-based governance and self-service of on-premises VMs need a replacement path before 2029. Check the source for Microsoft's recommended alternatives, such as per-machine Arc onboarding or Azure Local.

items.title: Retirement: Azure IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029
items.headline: Azure IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029
items.summary: Azure IoT Central, the managed IoT application platform, will be retired on September 20, 2029. Customers can keep using it until then but are advised to start transition planning early, as Microsoft refocuses its future IoT investment.
items.architecture_impact: Solutions built on IoT Central will need to move to a composed architecture, for example one built on IoT Hub with separate data and visualisation services, which brings more design and operations responsibility. Avoid IoT Central for new designs, and check the source for the recommended migration path.

items.title: SQL Server on Azure Local is now generally available
items.headline: SQL Server on Azure Local reaches general availability
items.summary: SQL Server can now run on Azure Local as a generally available offering. It targets customers who want to modernize while keeping control over infrastructure, connectivity and data placement. The item text is brief, so supported features, licensing and management integration need checking at the source.
items.architecture_impact: It adds a supported option for hosting relational data on-premises or at the edge under Azure management, relevant where residency, latency or disconnected-operation requirements rule out Azure SQL. Architects should compare HA, backup and management capabilities against Azure SQL Managed Instance and Azure Arc-enabled SQL Server before choosing a hybrid data platform.

items.title: [Launched] Generally Available: Vector search and vector indexes in Azure SQL
items.headline: Vector search and vector indexes are generally available in Azure SQL Database
items.summary: Azure SQL Database now offers GA approximate nearest neighbor vector search through CREATE VECTOR INDEX and VECTOR_SEARCH in T-SQL. It targets AI scenarios such as semantic search and RAG over data already held in Azure SQL.
items.architecture_impact: Architects can design RAG and semantic search directly on Azure SQL instead of syncing data to a separate vector store, which reduces data movement and keeps one security boundary. Weigh this against dedicated search services for scale and features, and check the source for index limits and performance characteristics.

items.headline: Several standalone Azure Communication Services offerings retire on 30 September 2028
items.summary: Microsoft will retire several standalone Azure Communication Services offerings on 30 September 2028, after which they will no longer be available. The feed text is truncated, so the exact list of affected services must be checked at the source.

items.title: [Launched] Generally Available: High-scale mesh in Azure Virtual Network Manager
items.headline: Azure Virtual Network Manager mesh now connects up to 3,000 VNets by default
items.summary: High-scale mesh using connected groups in Azure Virtual Network Manager is generally available in available regions. Customers can connect up to 3,000 virtual networks in a single mesh connectivity configuration by default, with higher scale possible. The full details are truncated and need checking at the source.
items.architecture_impact: Large estates can use direct VNet-to-VNet mesh at scale instead of relying only on hub-and-spoke transit, which reduces hub hops and dependence on the hub. Weigh this against centralized inspection and egress requirements, and check regional availability and the IP limits at the source.

items.title: Microsoft Foundry Observability: How to Trace, Evaluate, Monitor, and Secure AI Agents
items.headline: Observability for Foundry agents: tracing, evaluation, monitoring and alerting
items.summary: Using a refund agent that returns HTTP 200 while passing the wrong amount to a tool, the article argues that agent observability must cover five layers: technical, agent execution, safety/policy, quality and business outcome. It proposes Foundry Traces, Evaluation and Monitor for development and quality, Application Insights as the telemetry store, Log Analytics for KQL investigation and Azure Monitor alerts for response, all joined by OpenTelemetry.
items.architecture_impact: Traditional APM covers only the technical layer, so agent designs need tool-call arguments, policy checks and evaluation results captured as first-class telemetry. Standardising on OpenTelemetry spans for agent, model and tool calls keeps observability independent of any one agent framework, and Application Insights becomes the shared investigation surface.

items.title: Building on AI Landing Zones: Operationalizing Enterprise AI with the Citadel Architecture
items.headline: Citadel reference architecture for operating enterprise AI on landing zones and Foundry
items.summary: Citadel is an opinionated reference architecture for composing Microsoft Foundry and complementary Azure services into an enterprise AI operating model on top of AI landing zones. It separates shared governance (gateway-mediated model access, consumption attribution, cross-team observability, agent identity and ownership) from application-team workload environments, and recommends adopting it incrementally, one workload and one operational gap at a time.
items.architecture_impact: The key decisions are which resources are shared or isolated, where access policy is enforced (typically an API Management AI gateway), how usage is attributed per workload, and who owns onboarding, monitoring and incident response. Citadel complements existing landing-zone and Foundry investments rather than replacing them; preview status, feature availability and costs need checking per service.

items.title: [Launched] Generally Available: TLS/SSL certificate and end-to-end TLS encryption support for Azure Functions Flex Consumption
items.headline: Azure Functions Flex Consumption gains GA TLS/SSL certificates and end-to-end TLS
items.summary: Azure Functions Flex Consumption now supports TLS/SSL certificates through a new site-scoped certificate model, with end-to-end TLS encryption, generally available. Each function app can hold up to 3 private (.pfx) and 3 public (.cer) certificates, uploaded directly or imported from other sources (details truncated; check the source).
items.architecture_impact: Workloads that needed custom certificates or end-to-end TLS, for example client certificates or encrypted backend hops, can now run on Flex Consumption rather than Premium or App Service plans. Check that the per-app certificate limits fit your design.

items.title: Your Private Endpoint Does Not Cover Agent Egress: Locking Down Azure AI Foundry in Both Directions
items.headline: Locking down Azure AI Foundry both ways: private endpoint inbound, network injection out
items.summary: The article shows that a private endpoint with public access disabled secures only client-to-Foundry traffic, while agent calls out to tools such as an MCP server can still leave from Microsoft-owned public IPs. It walks through the inbound setup, which needs a custom domain and three private DNS zones linked through a zone group. Outbound traffic uses Standard Setup with bring-your-own VNet network injection on a subnet delegated to Microsoft.App/environments.
items.architecture_impact: Treat inbound and outbound isolation as separate design decisions, and prove both by testing for a 200 from inside the VNet and a 403 from outside. Network injection cannot be added to an existing Foundry account, so decide on private egress before deployment or plan a rebuild. Private networking forces Standard Setup with your own storage and other dependent resources.

items.title: Choosing the Right Agent in Microsoft Foundry
items.headline: Choosing prompt agents or hosted agents in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
items.summary: The article frames the choice as where orchestration logic lives. Prompt agents are declarative (model, instructions, tools) on a managed runtime and suit knowledge, review and self-service scenarios. Hosted agents run your own code in any framework, with Foundry managing the endpoint, identity, scaling and sessions, and suit branching, stateful, multi-agent or real-time workflows.
items.architecture_impact: Start with prompt agents for speed and governability. Move to hosted agents when instructions begin to look like application code, for example retries, state machines, custom payloads or deterministic business rules. The trade-off is more control in exchange for owning security patching, testing and runtime operations.

items.title: Token Economics in Practice
items.headline: Agent token economics: managing cost per accepted task with an Azure control loop
items.summary: Because agent runs are stochastic, the article argues for measuring cost per accepted task rather than token price, and for optimising expected cost under per-segment quality floors and a budget-breach probability. It pairs a pre-execution forecaster that produces P50/P95 planning estimates with a runtime governor. Policy is held in App Configuration and enforced through an API Management GenAI gateway; Foundry evaluations measure quality, and an Azure Monitor-triggered Function reverts unsafe cost policies.
items.architecture_impact: Cost controls such as routing, context trimming, caching and token limits should sit in a gateway with externalised policy, and should be tied to evaluation results so that savings which hurt quality are rolled back automatically. Treat forecast percentiles as planning estimates until they are calibrated against real traces.

items.title: Preserve a Legacy IP During Azure Migration with Private Link Service Direct Connect
items.headline: Keeping legacy dependency IPs during migration with Private Link Service Direct Connect
items.summary: For phased migrations where web and application tiers move to Azure but a database stays on premises behind a hard-coded private IP, the pattern places a Private Endpoint in the migrated VNet. That endpoint maps to a Private Link Service Direct Connect resource in a hub, which routes over site-to-site VPN to the on-premises address. The application keeps using the same address without code changes, even where address spaces overlap.
items.architecture_impact: This removes re-addressing from the critical path of the first migration wave and avoids VNet peering conflicts caused by overlapping address space. It is a bridge, not an end state. Direct Connect is in public preview in selected regions, so check requirements, limitations and regional availability before any production use.
